title: $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$ as the rationalization of $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\mathcal O_E)$
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and its ring of integers $\cO_E$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Let $X$ be a scheme whose underlying topological space is Noetherian. Use the pulled-back coefficient rings of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and the bounded constructible derived categories of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. There is an
equivalence of categories
$$
D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)[\ell^{-1}]\simeq D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)
$$
from the rationalization at the powers of $\ell$ [sk-def-sfb-rationalization]. Composed
with the localization functor
$Q\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)[\ell^{-1}]$,
it is isomorphic to $E\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\cO_E}-$, the functor of [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-extend-scalars].

proof.text: Set $\mathcal C=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$, $\mathcal D_1=\mathcal C[\ell^{-1}]$, $\mathcal D_2=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)$, and $L_1=Q$. Define $L_2\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D_2$ to be $\operatorname{boundedConstructibleExtendScalars}(X,\ell,E)$ of [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-extend-scalars]: the restriction of $L(\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi)=E_X\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\cO_{E,X}}-$, with the pulled-back coefficient morphism $\varphi\colon\cO_{E,X}\to E_X$. Thus $L_2$ is precisely the restricted functor denoted $E\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\cO_E}-$ in the item and in [thm-sfb-extend-scalars-localization]; no change of coefficient categories is involved. Take $W$ to consist of morphisms whose mapping cone is killed by some power $\ell^n$, $n\geq0$. Then $L_1$ is a localization for $W$ by [sk-def-sfb-rationalization], and $L_2$ is a localization for this same $W$ by [thm-sfb-extend-scalars-localization], since $X$ is topologically Noetherian.

By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], applied to the localization $Q\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D_1$ and the $W$-inverting functor $L_2$, choose $F\colon\mathcal D_1\to\mathcal D_2$ with a natural isomorphism $\alpha\colon F\circ Q\cong L_2$. Apply clause (1) again to the localization $L_2\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D_2$ and the $W$-inverting functor $Q$ to choose $G\colon\mathcal D_2\to\mathcal D_1$ with $\beta\colon G\circ L_2\cong Q$.

The composite $\beta\circ G(\alpha)$ is a natural isomorphism $G\circ F\circ Q\cong Q$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] with localization $Q$, functors $G\circ F\circ Q$ and $Q$ on $\mathcal C$, and their lifts $G\circ F$ and $\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal D_1}$, using the identity comparison isomorphisms (with the canonical associativity and identity identifications). These functors invert $W$ because $Q$ does and functors preserve isomorphisms. The composite therefore lifts to $G\circ F\cong\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal D_1}$. The composite $\alpha\circ F(\beta)$ is a natural isomorphism $F\circ G\circ L_2\cong L_2$. Apply clause (2) with localization $L_2$, functors $F\circ G\circ L_2$ and $L_2$, and their lifts $F\circ G$ and $\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal D_2}$, again with identity comparisons. These functors invert $W$ because $L_2$ does. This gives $F\circ G\cong\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal D_2}$. Thus $G$ is a quasiinverse of $F$, so $F$ is an equivalence, and $\alpha\colon F\circ Q\cong L_2$ is the required comparison.
